speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To better understand the severity and location of your nerve compression, can you tell me which specific fingers or thumb areas are affected by the paresthesias, and do you experience any numbness in your hand?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: Given your history of diabetes and the progressive weakness in both hands, have you noticed any difficulty with buttoning your shirt or holding objects, and is your neck pain worse when you look down or turn your head?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis).

The combination of progressive upper and lower motor neuron signs (weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes) in the context of burning pain and paresthesias strongly suggests a motor neuron disorder rather than a simple compression or infection. Given the previous misdiagnosis of a urinary tract infection, I need to confirm this immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Velocity, EMG, MRI_Cervical_Spine, Creatine_Kinase, Vitamin_B12_Level.
